subject: Re: Order form — pricing ladder, commit phasing & invoice routing
messages:
From: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme.com>

Cc: ProcureTeam <procure@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoice cadence & VAT classification

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the draft order form. Two quick items procurement needs clarity on before we can move to legal: 1) ACME prefers monthly invoicing where possible — can Redwood split the minimum commit into monthly invoices rather than a single upfront invoice? 2) For tax/VAT, which entity will issue the invoice and bear VAT (Redwood US or Redwood EMEA)? We need the invoice path for our AP team.

Attached is our procurement checklist; happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Luis
Procurement Manager — Acme Corp

Attachment: ACME_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice cadence & VAT classification

Hi Luis — thanks, and great questions. Quick answers up front: 1) We can split the committed amount into monthly invoices (we typically do tranche invoicing for multi-month commits) — see proposed schedule in the attached pricing-ladder-proposal.xlsx. 2) Redwood will invoice from our US entity by default for US customers; for EU customers we can route from Redwood EMEA which will impact VAT handling.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach an updated order form that adds a monthly invoice schedule and an appendix to state invoice entity (US vs EMEA) with a checkbox for AP to select.
- Looping in Kim (legal) and Ben (finance) to confirm there are no accounting or MSA implications for monthly tranches vs upfront billing and to confirm whether we need to change the net terms from our standard Net45 to Net60 for this ACME deployment.

If that sounds ok I’ll share updated Order Form for signature.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-ladder-proposal.xlsx, ACME_OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice cadence & VAT classification

Thanks for the context. My quick read on legal is: monthly invoices are fine from a contract standpoint, but we need to capture two things explicitly in the order form and MSA redline: 1) "Invoice Trigger" language (what constitutes billable usage tied to commit tranches) — avoids disputes about activation timing, and 2) "Tax Allocation" clause that states invoicing entity and whether Redwood will gross up or pass through VAT.

A few asks for ops/finance:
- Ben: can finance confirm whether we can support monthly invoices for the min-commit and how that maps to revenue recognition (stated as "deferred revenue vs immediate recognition" in accounting speak)?
- Stephanie: please mark whether ACME expects PO numbers on each monthly invoice or a single PO that covers the full commit. If they expect separate POs per invoice we'll need invoice numbering alignment.

I attached suggested wording in the order form redlines (see ACME_OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf). I highlighted the Tax Allocation clause and a recommended fallback that Redwood invoices from the US entity unless customer identifies EMEA entity and provides valid VAT registration.

—Kim

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice cadence & VAT classification

Quick finance note: monthly tranche invoicing is operationally fine. Two points: 1) For ACME’s case, if they want monthly invoices for the minimum commit we will set up each tranche as a separate invoice and apply the PO (or a single cross-referenced PO) — both are supported but the PO-per-invoice route increases AP reconciliation work on both sides. 2) Net terms: finance prefers Net45 (our standard) for customers with no credit exception; if procurement is asking for Net60 we can evaluate but would prefer to compensate via a smaller deferred revenue schedule or a commitment ladder that front-loads a larger tranche in month 1.

I recommend we offer: monthly invoices + Net45 standard, with an option for Net60 subject to credit approval. Also confirm whether ACME requires Redwood to gross up for VAT — if so, we'll need pricing impact approval.

—Ben

From: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, ProcureTeam <procure@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice cadence & VAT classification

Thanks — that all helps. ACME preference: monthly invoices (PO on file that covers full commit, but we can reference the PO number per invoice), Net60 is preferred but we can accept Net45 during onboarding if Redwood adds the Net60 ask to the SOW and we keep it under review. For VAT: we’ll provide Redwood with our EU VAT registration if we decide to route invoice to the EMEA entity; otherwise we’ll accept invoices from Redwood US and handle VAT per our local rules.

Can you please send the updated order form with the Invoice Trigger language and Tax Allocation clause included? Also we need a short doc that our tax team can use to confirm Redwood’s invoice entity (little checklist is fine).

Best,
Luis
